item.title: YFG Fatso Waives Extradition To Georgia After Chicago Hearing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: YFG Fatso waived extradition to Georgia after a Chicago hearing, a report said. The underlying Georgia offense was not identified.
item.content:encoded:
YFG Fatso waived extradition to Georgia at a November 2 hearing in Chicago, according to Chicago Crime Chaser, which reported that the rapper faced a warrant from that state.

The 19-year-old artist, whose legal name is Christopher C. Mosley, was booked in Cook County on October 29 on a local fugitive hold tied to the Georgia warrant.

Judge Rivanda Doss Beal handled the hearing at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. The report said local prosecutors dropped the fugitive hold, but a custody order kept him awaiting pickup by Georgia authorities.

The account did not identify the underlying Georgia offense or establish that a transfer had taken place. It also did not say where he was.

Fatso had discussed an earlier period of house arrest on “Off The Porch.” The October 2025 episode description said he had recently come off house arrest then. That account preceded this week’s extradition proceedings by more than a year.

That appearance also covered making his first song at 13 and getting attention from the video for “Go Go.” He discussed his first connection to Lil Durk through Lil King and signing with OTF.

His album Sanity Evaded arrived July 9 through YFG Fatso/Santa Anna, following 2024’s A Reaper’s Ceremony.

The 18-song release ran 53 minutes and featured Rob49 on “Clean Up Crew” and Tee Grizzley on “They Need Me.”

item.title: Jeffrey Wright Calls W.E.B. Du Bois Documentary One Of His Proudest Projects
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jeffrey Wright calls W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause one of his proudest projects as Rita Coburn's documentary tours.
item.content:encoded:
Jeffrey Wright is placing his work on W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause among the projects that mean the most to him as Rita Coburn’s documentary continues its screening tour.

“I do a lot of stuff, but I’m not prouder of any other piece that I’ve been a part of than this,” Wright said during a conversation about the film.

Wright performs dramatic readings from Du Bois’ writing in the two-hour American Masters documentary. Viola Davis narrates, while Common and Courtney B. Vance also give voice to Du Bois’ words.

The role asked Wright to serve the language rather than turn the scholar into a character.

Coburn built the film around Du Bois’ books, speeches, journalism, archival audio and the voices of historians who explain why his work still lands.

Wright said the finished movie exceeded what he expected.

“I watched it and was just blown away by the beauty of the film and by the comprehensiveness of the narrative arc,” he told People earlier this year.

The film follows Du Bois from his 1868 birth in Massachusetts through the collapse of Reconstruction, two world wars and the rise of the modern Civil Rights Movement.

He co-founded the NAACP, helped launch the Niagara Movement and used scholarship, journalism and data to expose racial inequality.

Du Bois also challenged Booker T. Washington and Marcus Garvey, and his 1903 book The Souls of Black Folk delivered the warning that “the problem of the twentieth century is the color line.”

Coburn’s film does not flatten that history into a victory lap. It covers his political battles, internationalism and personal losses, including the death of his infant son.

Du Bois died in Ghana on August 27, 1963, one day before the March on Washington.

“My hope is that this documentary invites reflection and sparks dialogue, not only about who Du Bois was,” Coburn said on the official film page.

The documentary premiered on PBS in May and later traveled to theaters and community screenings.

A London event in October paired the movie with a conversation featuring Coburn and Wright. Screenings in Los Angeles and New York are scheduled for November 12 and November 19.

For Wright, the project connects a foundational Black thinker to the present without sanding down the force of his ideas. His pride comes from helping Du Bois’ own words remain the center of the story.

item.title: Kodak Black Likeness Appears In New GTA VI Launch Gallery
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kodak Black appears in Rockstar's new GTA VI launch gallery, though the studio has not identified his apparent character.
item.content:encoded:
Kodak Black appears to have entered Leonida, with his likeness turning up in Rockstar Games’ new Grand Theft Auto VI launch gallery.

Rockstar released the collection Thursday (November 5), exactly two weeks before the game arrives on November 19. “Grand Theft Auto VI is now officially only two weeks away,” the company said in its announcement.

Viewers quickly zeroed in on one figure whose face tattoos, hair and 1800 Block chain closely resemble the Pompano Beach rapper. The details immediately led to claims that the image shows Kodak rather than a loose parody or an unrelated character.

An important line still exists between recognition and confirmation. Rockstar’s gallery does not name the figure.

The company has not announced whether Kodak voices anyone, appears as himself, plays a fictional character or is part of a single scene. Kodak Black has not publicly spelled out his role either.

Rockstar has kept much of the game’s voice cast secret, which makes the missing credit meaningful rather than conclusive.

His connection to the game is not coming out of nowhere. Kodak’s older music was previously confirmed for GTA VI, putting his voice in the game’s Florida-inspired world before the new image surfaced. Rockstar has also leaned heavily into regional music and culture while building Vice City and the wider state of Leonida.

The music rollout is a separate piece of that world. Rockstar announced a 34-track album of new music for launch day, with early singles from Future and Metro Boomin, Travis Scott, PinkPantheress, Rauw Alejandro, Morgan Wallen and Keith Richards. That announcement did not describe Kodak’s apparent on-screen presence.

The gallery arrives after a quieter legal stretch for Kodak, whose real name is Bill Kapri. In September, Florida prosecutors declined to file charges in an Orange County MDMA case, saying the evidence was insufficient to prove possession.

A Broward judge also dismissed a separate fleeing-and-eluding charge that month.

For now, the launch gallery supports a careful conclusion: a figure designed to look like Kodak Black is in Rockstar’s official GTA VI imagery. The size and nature of his role remain undisclosed ahead of the November 19 release.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony, La La Reportedly Reach Divorce Settlement After 9 Years
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Carmelo Anthony and La La Anthony reportedly reached a settlement in their divorce case more than five years after the filing.
item.content:encoded:
Carmelo Anthony and La La Anthony have reportedly taken a major step toward closing a divorce case that has stretched on for more than nine years.

According to court records cited by TMZ, the former couple informed the court that they had reached a settlement.

The available report did not disclose the terms or say that a judge had entered a final divorce judgment.

That distinction matters. A reported settlement can resolve the issues between the parties, but it is not the same as confirmation that the marriage has been legally dissolved.

For now, the supported development is that Carmelo and La La appear to have worked out an agreement after a long-running case.

La La filed for divorce in June 2021 after 11 years of marriage. The filing followed years of strain.

They separated in 2017, appeared to reconcile in 2018 and later moved toward ending the marriage. They share a son, Kiyan Anthony.

By the time La La filed, she had already been living with the emotional fallout of the separation for years.

During a 2021 appearance on “The Angie Martinez Show,” she described the split as painful and public while saying she and Carmelo had reached a good place as co-parents.

She also sounded deeply uncertain about marrying again.

“Marriage, I don’t think I can do that ever again. I mean, some amazing person would have to come. I don’t see that happening again,” La La said.

The timeline helps explain why the reported settlement is significant. The public divorce filing came four years after their first separation, and the case then remained unresolved for more than five additional years.

Their ability to co-parent amicably did not mean the legal process had reached its end.

The divorce was still part of La La’s public conversation days before the settlement report.

Neither the limited settlement report nor the available court-record summary provided financial terms, parenting terms or a date for a final judgment.

It also did not include a new public statement from Carmelo or La La.

That leaves the case’s final status unclear, even with an agreement reportedly in place.

What the new report does show is movement in a case that had remained open since La La’s 2021 filing.

Until a final judgment is confirmed, the settlement should be described as a reported agreement, not a completed divorce.

item.title: Texas Attorney General-Elect Nathan Johnson Scored 67 Dragon Ball Z Episodes
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nathan Johnson won the Texas attorney general race after an earlier career scoring 67 Dragon Ball Z episodes and five films.
item.content:encoded:
Texas attorney general-elect Nathan Johnson is heading into one of the most powerful law-enforcement jobs in the country with a résumé no other state prosecutor can match: he scored 67 episodes of Dragon Ball Z and five of the franchise’s films.

Johnson, a Democrat from Dallas, won the statewide race Tuesday (November 3) against Republican Mayes Middleton.

The victory made him the first Democrat elected Texas attorney general since 1994, but the anime chapter of his career quickly became the part of his biography that traveled far beyond political circles.

Long before Johnson entered the Texas Senate, he worked on music for Funimation’s English-language version of Dragon Ball Z. His film credits included The World’s Strongest, The Tree of Might, Broly — Second Coming, Fusion Reborn and Wrath of the Dragon.

The work also gave Johnson an unexpected bond with his young son.

“I remember him sitting on my knee and stuff blowing up,” Johnson recalled. “He was like, ‘Oh, Daddy, Goku!'”

He later described the job as a “creative outlet and a cultural connection.”

That background was not a campaign gimmick. Johnson studied physics at the University of Arizona before earning his law degree from the University of Texas at Austin.

He built a career as a litigator and mediator, then won his Texas Senate seat in 2018 and took office in 2019.

His official Senate biography credits him with work on the state’s electrical grid, healthcare access, government transparency, criminal justice and infrastructure.

His campaign biography says he authored roughly 433 bills and passed 134 into law across four legislative sessions.

Those issues will matter far more to his new office than anime music, but the combination explains why his election story reached culture pages as quickly as political ones.

Johnson is expected to succeed Republican Ken Paxton, who left the attorney general’s race to seek a U.S. Senate seat.

The attorney general oversees major civil litigation, consumer protection, child-support enforcement and legal representation for the state, putting Johnson’s courtroom experience at the center of his next job.

The Dragon Ball Z credits remain a revealing piece of that route.

Before statewide office and legislative battles, Johnson was writing music for scenes built around transformation, survival and impossible fights. Now the former composer will bring a very different kind of score sheet into the Texas attorney general’s office.

item.title: Javits Frimpong’s Family Receives Nearly $900,000 As Parents Seek Justice
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Javits Frimpong inspired an extraordinary wave of generosity as bereaved loved ones demand justice.
item.content:encoded:
Javits Frimpong’s family received nearly $900,000 in donations after the Ghanaian teenager’s walk to school in the Bronx ended in a fatal shooting.

The 15-year-old’s death has brought financial support and public mourning as his parents seek answers about the Oct. 29 attack. A GoFundMe benefiting his father, Thomas Frimpong, showed $898,199 toward a $1.1 million goal Thursday, Nov. 5, with more than 27,000 donations. The campaign will help cover funeral costs, burial arrangements and unexpected expenses. 

READ ALSO: Cardi B Calls Out “Rage Bait” Over Javits Frimpong’s Killing

His mother, Doris Adu Gyamfi, traveled from Ghana toward New York on Wednesday after receiving a visa to attend her son’s funeral. Video released by Ghana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs showed relatives praying before boarding their flight, ABC7 reported. 

Javits had moved to the United States to join his father just a year earlier. According to the family’s fundraiser, Oct. 28 marked the anniversary of his arrival. He was killed the following morning while heading to DreamYard Preparatory School. 

Investigators said three people wearing hoods and surgical masks were in Crotona Park before approaching Javits. He ran and all three pursued him before he was shot in the back, NYPD Chief of Detectives Joseph Kenny said. Javits later died at the hospital.

Thomas believes the killing was connected to bullying. He said the school principal had informed him that two students were suspended following an incident involving his son.

“The principal told me Javits is innocent. Javits is innocent. He was defending himself,” Thomas said.

Police are examining bullying as a possible motive but have not established that connection. Kenny said investigators were also considering robbery and mistaken identity. He said detectives had found no indication that Javits was involved in gang activity.

Questions have also surrounded access to school records. Kenny said Monday that the Department of Education required a subpoena before releasing information about the alleged bullying. The department subsequently said it was cooperating and would provide records in accordance with applicable laws. 

Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Oct. 31 that President Donald Trump had agreed to grant Javits’ mother a visa immediately following their telephone conversation. Her departure Wednesday brought the family closer to gathering for his funeral. 

“I want justice for my son, that’s all. I wanted my son to become a doctor,” his mother said in a video.

The donations will help the family bury Javits. His mother’s words describe the future she had imagined for him: an education followed by a medical career. As supporters contribute toward his funeral, his parents are still seeking answers about the morning that ended those plans.

item.title: FG Famous Released From Federal Prison Then Arrested Hours Later
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: FG Famous left federal custody on November 2, only to be booked hours later in Louisiana's separate racketeering case.
item.content:encoded:
JaydaYoungin’s brother FG Famous was released from federal custody on November 2 after serving nearly all of a five-year sentence, then booked hours later in Louisiana on a separate racketeering charge.

The Bogalusa rapper, whose legal name is Mark Amos IV, entered the Washington Parish jail at 11:41 p.m., according to booking information. The new arrest returns Amos to a state case that was pending while he served his federal term.

A Washington Parish grand jury indicted Amos and 15 other people in February 2024. Prosecutors accused the group of participating in a racketeering enterprise that operated between January 2017 and November 2023.

The state indictment arrived while Amos was still moving through the federal case. That timing left two different tracks: a federal conviction with a fixed prison term, and a Louisiana prosecution that could continue after his release. The November booking reflects the second track, not a new federal sentence.

The 22nd Judicial District Attorney’s Office said the alleged enterprise involved a network tied to firearms and narcotics. The indictment release described a wider collection of alleged crimes by members and associates, including murder, attempted murder, kidnapping, money laundering and obstruction.

Those allegations were made against the alleged enterprise as a whole; the release listed Amos on the racketeering count without assigning every alleged act to him.

Then-Interim District Attorney J. Collin Sims called it “part of a series of indictments targeting violent crime in Bogalusa with our local, state, and federal partners.”

Amos’ federal case came from a July 2022 police pursuit. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, officers tried to stop a Corvette he was driving, but he sped through a residential area at more than 100 mph before fleeing on foot and hiding beneath a nearby house.

Officers said a backpack near Amos contained about 522 grams of marijuana and two 9mm handguns, including one reported stolen. He later pleaded guilty to possessing a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime.

A federal judge sentenced Amos in August 2024 to 60 months in prison, three years of supervised release and a $100 assessment. His November 2 booking does not erase that completed federal sentence. It places him back in custody as Louisiana prosecutors continue the separate racketeering case.

item.title: Mona Love Apologizes To Cardi B And Admits She Failed To Research Clip
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mona Love apologized to Cardi B and admitted poor research turned an edited 2024 clip into an avoidable colorism fight.
item.content:encoded:
Mona Love apologized to Cardi B after admitting she built a public colorism argument around an edited clip from an old video without doing enough research.

Love addressed the mess during Episode 978 of “The Joe Budden Podcast,” released Wednesday (November 4). She joined by phone after Joe Budden said the cast didn’t want to discuss her while she was absent.

The comedian said she reached out to Cardi after the rapper responded and never meant to hurt her. What hit Love hardest was Cardi’s claim that the discussion had brought another wave of attacks her way.

“Like that shit makes me feel horrible,” Love said.

Love said she had been dragged online herself and would not wish that experience on anyone. She added that hearing Cardi connect the backlash to her comments made her feel bad, especially because Cardi had been kind to her during years of private contact.

Budden told Love that the broader discussion about colorism did not need Cardi as its central example. He also reminded her that a platform as large as theirs carries real weight, even when a speaker’s intent is different from the result.

Love accepted that point. She said her reaction would have been completely different if she had known the clip was edited or understood how old it was.

She also admitted this was not the first time she had spoken on the podcast without researching enough. Her lesson was simple: “This was avoidable.”

The apology followed a sharp public response from Cardi on November 2. AllHipHop previously reported that the Bronx rapper said a 13-second section of a 15-minute Instagram Live from 2024 had been stripped of context.

Cardi said she had never denied that colorism was real or that lighter-skinned women could gain access to some opportunities.

Her objection was the idea that complexion explained her career. Cardi pointed to the work, talent and strategy behind her success.

She also questioned why Love had not contacted her privately about the clip after seeking her advice over the years on personal matters, surgery, career moves and brand deals.

Love had argued that Cardi’s lighter skin and Dominican heritage could affect how brands and the entertainment business viewed her.

She said her point was about unequal access, not a lack of talent. The problem, she now acknowledged, was focusing on Cardi without checking the full source.

Love said she and Cardi had already exchanged messages privately. She would not reveal what was said, but she promised to repeat her apology on a large platform instead of keeping it inside a direct message.

She said the episode forced her to tighten up her research before weighing in on another public dispute.

item.title: Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean Open Fugees Hopeline With New Music And Fan Messages
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean launched Fugees Hopeline, inviting fans to hear new music and share messages for a global art project.
item.content:encoded:
Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean opened a phone line that lets fans hear new Fugees music, leave their own messages of hope and potentially become part of an art presentation in Miami Beach.

The pair launched Fugees Hopeline with public art platform CIRCA on November 5, alongside three original collages created by Hill.

The project expanded their celebration of the 30th anniversary of The Score beyond the concert stage.

Hill’s daughter Selah Marley narrated the experience. Callers can hear personal messages from Hill and Jean, get a first listen to a new Fugees medley and record their own stories.

Those contributions will build an international audio archive.

“We’ve been able to connect with people from around the world through our music. We’ve shared stories from our lives, and visions for the future,” Hill and Jean said in a joint statement.

The invitation puts listeners’ experiences at the center of the project, with the artists asking people to explain what hope means in their own lives.

“With FUGEES HOPELINE, we want to hear everyone else’s stories. Hope means something different to everyone. Sometimes it’s finding beauty in a difficult moment, sometimes it’s choosing kindness, and sometimes it’s simply knowing that your voice matters. Our dream is that this project creates a space for people to share their wisdom, stories, connect and remind us all the power of our shared humanity.”

Fans in the United States can call +1 (424) 738-4337. International participants can reach the same number through WhatsApp.

The idea drew inspiration from John Giorno’s Dial-A-Poem, which used the telephone to bring recorded poetry to listeners.

The number will appear throughout November on London’s Piccadilly Lights, the Marriott L.A. Live screen in downtown Los Angeles and other international locations.

“Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean are voices of a generation, and with FUGEES HOPELINE, the microphone is now being passed to the public,” CIRCA founder and artistic director Josef O’Connor said.

CIRCA commissioned the audio work while also publishing Hill’s collages. The pieces combine photographs, typography and archival images from three decades of Fugees history.

“Together, we’re inviting people around the world to explore, question and redefine what hope means in our time, creating a collective sonic record of life in 2026. This ambitious new commission continues CIRCA’s mission to expand the boundaries of public art, bringing together music, visual culture and collective participation. From Piccadilly Lights to the Fugees’ US tour, FUGEES HOPELINE connects audiences across borders, transforming the telephone into a space for reflection, expression and human connection.”

The visual work includes photographs by B+, Angela Thomas, Ricardo de Rozario, Hideo and Jonathan Mannion. Large A2 prints, hand-signed by Hill and Jean, are limited to 500 of each design and cost about $1,350 each or about $3,370 for all three.

Smaller A4 stamp-signed prints cost about $270 each or about $675 for the set. Orders run from November 1 through December 31, with the number sold determining that edition’s final size.

Hill had already worked with CIRCA on a public art presentation in August.

She curated Lauren Halsey’s work for Piccadilly Lights as part of the wider Diaspora Calling! celebration, which brought music, visual art and community events together.

The new launch followed Hill and Jean’s November 4 anniversary show at Berkeley’s Greek Theatre. Their announced dates continue in Las Vegas on November 6, Los Angeles on November 8 and Seattle on November 10.

Selected Hopeline recordings are planned for presentation at Faena Forum in Miami Beach on December 4 and 5 during Art Basel Miami Beach.

Hill will curate the exhibition in collaboration with Saint Citizen.

item.title: Montell Jordan Reveals Q Parker Showed Up For Almost Every Cancer Treatment
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Montell Jordan recalled Q Parker's early morning hospital visits during cancer treatment and the support his wife helped arrange.
item.content:encoded:
Montell Jordan said Q Parker drove an hour early in the morning to support him and his wife through nearly all of his second round of cancer treatments.

On “R&B Money,” Jordan estimated that Parker attended 32 or 33 of his 37 proton therapy appointments at Emory in Atlanta. The visits ran five days a week for seven and a half weeks.

Jordan shared the story with hosts Tank and J. Valentine in an interview.

His wife, Kristin, had asked friends to help. She also gathered relatives and prayer partners to support them. Parker arrived for the first treatment and then committed to returning.

“I want to be here,” Parker told him, Jordan recalled.

That meant leaving around 5 or 6 A.M. to cross town and meet the couple at the hospital.

“That man didn’t have to do that, man,” he said.

His first prostate cancer diagnosis followed a routine test in early 2024. He underwent prostate removal surgery and announced that he was cancer-free before that year ended.

Months after that November surgery, doctors found cancer again. As AllHipHop previously reported, follow-up testing in 2025 found cancer in the prostate bed and lymph nodes on Jordan’s left side.

That recurrence brought a new treatment plan, including radiation and hormone therapy. Jordan was documenting the experience for “Sustain.” He kept making public appearances during treatment, telling an audience that he had flown out after finishing a week of appointments.

“I have six more weeks of the treatment that I’m taking right now,” he said in that October 2025 update.

By February 2026, the singer had shared a different update. In an exclusive interview with People, he said he had learned on Christmas Day 2025 that he was cancer-free.

“Christmas Day we found out that we are undetected, cancer-free,” Jordan said.

He also credited Kristin, whom he married in 1994, for the support she gave him through both diagnoses. “She supported me and carried me,” he told People.

The support also changed how Jordan viewed his ties to music.

“So music may have loved me in ways that I didn’t know.”
